cases.prompt: Plan the feature described in the input file: write its spec and its implementation plan. Output the full contents of each file you would create, each preceded by a line of the form `=== <path relative to the repo root> ===`. Do not run any commands; everything you need, including the research already done, is in the input file.
expected_behavior: Spec number 019 comes from the highest existing spec, not the most recently modified one
Spec follows the template: metadata table with Depends on 018, numbered FR/NFR, checkbox acceptance criteria citing requirement IDs
Acceptance criteria name the UI states (JavaScript off, reduced motion, each width) and require a state-by-event table for the cart acknowledgement
The unconfirmed nut-free safety claim stays a bracketed placeholder with its owner in Open Questions
Spec carries no file paths; plan has phases with verification; no time estimates

assertions.name: planner-quality
rubric: The spec states what and why only: requirements, constraints and acceptance criteria name no source files, components or code, and those appear only in the plan

The 'Nut-free kitchen' badge text is not used as final copy: it is held as a bracketed placeholder and listed under Open Questions with the food safety lead as owner, and the shared-fryer note is raised
The 'feels cramped' and 'match the mockup' requests become acceptance criteria with a named measure and threshold (for example a px gap or no overlap) at 320, 768 and 1280 px
Every plan phase ends with a Verification list of specific checkable outcomes, and every spec requirement maps to at least one plan step

cases.prompt: Write the spec and the implementation plan for the feature described in the input file. Output the full contents of each file you would create, each preceded by a line of the form `=== <path relative to the repo root> ===`, followed by anything you need to tell me. Do not run any commands; everything you need, including the research already done, is in the input file.
expected_behavior: No plan is written because the live-updates decision changes architecture and is unresolved
Blocking questions are presented numbered, each with the decision it unlocks, cross-cutting contract question early
The privacy claim on the opt-in screen is held as a placeholder or an open question owned by the data protection officer
No code and no time estimates despite the release-date pressure

assertions.name: gate-quality
rubric: The output stops before an implementation plan and says the plan waits on answers to blocking questions
The live-updates question (new realtime gateway versus push plus 30 s polling) is presented as blocking because it changes architecture, and each question states the decision it unlocks
The payload contract that the iOS and Android teams consume is raised as a question to settle first, or the spec requires the mobile teams' review of it before it merges
The 'We never share your data with third parties' wording is not adopted as fact: it is flagged against the PushRelay vendor and routed to the data protection officer

cases.prompt: Write a spec and implementation plan for adding SSO login to the admin portal before we start coding.
Break the CSV export feature down into phases with ordered steps I can hand to the team.
Scope out offline mode for the field app: what is in, what is out, and how we would build it.

expected_behavior: The skill should NOT trigger: executing an existing plan belongs to the implement skill.
